title: Check: the network model
description: Five questions on the flat network and the plugin that provides it.

questions.prompt: Which rules does the Kubernetes network model require? Choose all that apply.

options.text: Every Pod gets its own IP address
Pods can reach each other without NAT
Agents on a node can reach all Pods on that node

questions.explanation: Those three are the contract every CNI plugin must satisfy. Encryption is a plugin feature, not part of the model.

options.text: A CNI plugin such as Calico, Cilium or Flannel

questions.explanation: The CNI plugin gives Pods addresses and makes pod-to-pod traffic work. kube-proxy handles Service VIPs, which is a different job.

questions.prompt: A fresh kubeadm cluster leaves every node NotReady. Why?

options.text: No CNI plugin is installed, so NetworkReady is false

questions.explanation: Expected behaviour, not a broken cluster. `kubectl describe node` shows the condition in plain words.

options.text: The range Services are allocated from
The range Pod IPs are allocated from

questions.explanation: `--pod-network-cidr` at kubeadm init must agree with what the CNI plugin expects, or Pods get addresses nothing routes.

questions.prompt: Two containers in one Pod communicate over what?

options.text: localhost, because they share a network namespace

questions.explanation: One IP per Pod. Containers inside it share the namespace, so they must not both bind the same port.
